findings.title: Command Injection via Unsanitized Input
findings.description: Tool accepts user input passed directly to shell execution without proper sanitization.

remediation.description: Use shlex.quote() to escape user input, use argument lists instead of shell strings, implement a command allowlist.
remediation.code_example:
# Safe: use argument list
subprocess.run(["ls", shlex.quote(user_input)])

findings.reason: Tool accepts user input passed directly to shell execution without proper sanitization.

findings.title: System Prompt Injection Vector in User Input Path
findings.description: User-controlled input is concatenated directly into system prompts or agent instructions without sanitization. This enables Agent Goal Hijack (ASI-01) where attackers can redirect the agent's planning and objectives.

location.snippet:
prompt += f'

There was an error with the request.
Error: {e}

Please reformat GraphQL query (avoid issues with backticks if possible).'

remediation.description: Never concatenate user input directly into system prompts. Use structured prompt templates with clear separation between system instructions and user data. Implement input validation and sanitization before passing to any prompt template.
remediation.code_example:
# BAD: Direct concatenation
prompt = f"You are an agent. User says: {user_input}"

# GOOD: Structured separation
messages = [
    SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful agent."),
    HumanMessage(content=sanitize(user_input))
]

findings.reason: User-controlled input is concatenated directly into system prompts or agent instructions without sanitization. This enables Agent Goal Hijack (ASI-01) where attackers can redirect the agent's planning and objectives.

findings.title: Unsandboxed Code Execution in Agent
findings.description: Agent executes dynamically generated code (via eval, exec, subprocess, or code interpreter tools) without sandbox isolation. This enables RCE attacks where manipulated prompts lead to arbitrary code execution on the host system (ASI-05).

remediation.description: NEVER execute LLM-generated code on the host system without hardware-enforced sandbox isolation. Use Docker containers with read-only filesystems, disabled networking, and resource limits. Apply static analysis to generated code before execution.

findings.reason: Agent executes dynamically generated code (via eval, exec, subprocess, or code interpreter tools) without sandbox isolation. This enables RCE attacks where manipulated prompts lead to arbitrary code execution on the host system (ASI-05).

findings.title: No Error Handling in Tool Execution
findings.description: Agent tool functions lack error handling, causing unhandled exceptions to propagate and potentially trigger cascading failures across the agent's execution pipeline (ASI-08).

remediation.description: Wrap all tool function bodies in try/except with graceful error messages. Never let raw exceptions propagate to the agent planner.

findings.title: SQL Injection via String Interpolation
findings.description: SQL queries are constructed using f-strings, .format(), string concatenation, or % formatting instead of parameterized queries. This allows SQL injection attacks through user-controlled input.

remediation.description: Use parameterized queries instead of string interpolation. Pass user input as separate parameters, not as part of the SQL string.
remediation.code_example:
# BAD: SQL injection vulnerable
cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = '{user_id}'")
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s" % user_id)

# GOOD: Parameterized query
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,))

findings.reason: SQL queries are constructed using f-strings, .format(), string concatenation, or % formatting instead of parameterized queries. This allows SQL injection attacks through user-controlled input.
